clinicalPearls: The least common but most severe of the classic stromal dystrophies, and the only one inherited in an autosomal recessive pattern
Caused by mutations in the CHST6 gene, which encodes a carbohydrate sulfotransferase needed for normal keratan sulfate sulfation
Deposits are glycosaminoglycan (abnormal keratan sulfate) accumulations staining with Alcian blue and colloidal iron on histology
Opacities are ill-defined greyish-white spots with cloudy intervening stroma extending limbus to limbus and full thickness, unlike the clear stroma seen between granular deposits
The diffuse stromal haze and full-thickness, edge-to-edge involvement cause earlier and more marked visual loss than granular or lattice dystrophy
Corneal thinning and endothelial involvement can occur, distinguishing it from other stromal dystrophies
The systemic mucopolysaccharidoses are an important differential for stromal clouding and should be excluded when there are systemic features
Management centres on lamellar or penetrating keratoplasty for advanced disease, with lubrication and erosion care as adjuncts
reference.pathophysiology: Macular corneal dystrophy is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the CHST6 gene encoding a corneal N-acetylglucosamine-6-O-sulfotransferase. Defective sulfation of keratan sulfate leads to accumulation of abnormal, poorly soluble glycosaminoglycan within keratocytes, the extracellular stroma, and the endothelium. This deposition, together with diffuse clouding of the intervening stroma, spreads from limbus to limbus and through the full corneal thickness, progressively degrading transparency. Because the defect involves a systemic sulfation pathway that is clinically confined to the cornea, deposits accumulate throughout the stroma rather than in discrete islands.
additionalDifferentials: Congenital hereditary stromal or endothelial dystrophy
Diffuse stromal scarring from prior keratitis
Interstitial keratitis with residual stromal haze
additionalInvestigations: Slit-lamp examination documenting diffuse full-thickness stromal clouding limbus to limbus
Histology with Alcian blue and colloidal iron staining of glycosaminoglycan deposits
CHST6 genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Pachymetry, as the cornea is often abnormally thin
Systemic and urinary glycosaminoglycan evaluation when a mucopolysaccharidosis is suspected
Specular microscopy to assess endothelial involvement before surgery
redFlags: Early and progressive visual loss from diffuse stromal clouding
Systemic features suggesting an underlying mucopolysaccharidosis rather than isolated corneal disease
Corneal thinning increasing the risk of perforation or surgical complication
Endothelial dysfunction contributing to oedema and graft failure risk
reference.prognosis: Macular dystrophy tends to progress earlier and more severely than other stromal dystrophies, often requiring keratoplasty by early adulthood. Grafts can restore useful vision, though recurrence in the graft is possible over time.
pitfalls: Assuming autosomal dominant inheritance and missing the recessive pattern and family risk
Failing to exclude systemic mucopolysaccharidosis when stromal clouding is present
Underestimating corneal thinning and endothelial involvement before surgery
Mistaking diffuse haze for scarring from previous inflammation
references: Cornea by Krachmer, Mannis and Holland
management: Keratoplasty is the definitive treatment, with penetrating or deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty typically required by early adulthood for visual rehabilitation
Optical management in earlier disease with refractive correction and rigid gas-permeable contact lenses to optimise vision before surgery
Symptomatic relief of photophobia and surface discomfort with ocular lubricants and tinted lenses
Pre-operative specular microscopy and pachymetry to assess endothelial involvement and corneal thinning, guiding choice of lamellar versus penetrating graft
Long-term post-graft surveillance for graft recurrence, rejection and thin-cornea complications
Multidisciplinary corneal specialist care with CHST6 genetic confirmation
Genetic counselling and family screening given the autosomal recessive inheritance
